title: POC Weekly Sync - onboarding & env readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review onboarding progress, access and env readiness, initial benchmark results, and next steps to run a production-like test. VPC peering and KMS setup in progress; Redwood to share updated benchmark sheet and SOC2 docs. Agreed to run latency-focused tests with a 500 reqs sample and confirm dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs.
topics: Access setup: VPC peering, IAM roles, KMS/HSM keys
Environment readiness: test dataset, staging infra, sample traffic patterns
Benchmark results: latency, throughput, token cost; model variants and quantization
Next steps: action owners and timelines, security docs and pilot plan
action_items: Ethan: Finish VPC peering request and send peering ID to Priya - due 2026-04-02
Sofia: Confirm KMS key ACLs for Redwood and provide key ARN - due 2026-04-01
Jordan: Share updated benchmark spreadsheet and runbook link - due 2026-03-31
Priya: Kick off 500-req latency test on staging and upload raw logs - due 2026-04-06
Maya: Provide 200 sample prompt set for eval (PII scrubbed) - due 2026-04-03
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + security questionnaire link
Schedule in-prod smoke test week of 2026-04-12 pending env readiness
Align on cost targets for dedicated vs hosted by next sync
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give it a quick 45 min sync today, focus on access and the preliminary bench marks and then next steps, um, I think Priya has the numbers.
[00:22] Priya Menon: yeah hi all, uh quick agenda: VPC peering status, KMS, staging test run, and the latency/throughput results from last night's run.
[00:38] Maya Patel: Cool, um also want to confirm stakeholders, we have engineering and security on the line.
[00:45] Ethan Ross: Ethan here, we raised the peering ticket yesterday, but need the subnet ranges from Redwood.
[00:51] Jordan Lee: Right, I sent the CIDR ranges in the thread, sorry if that got buried, it's 10.10.0.0/16 for the staging cluster.
[01:02] Ethan Ross: ok I'll plug that in. Quick question on routing - do you expect boto to run in our VPC or is it a cross-account setup?
[01:14] Priya Menon: It's cross-account peering; Redwood will run a private endpoint in your VPC and we'll do peering plus route table entries. Should be straight forward but we do need the peering id once you create it.
[01:30] Sofia Li: From security, we need the KMS workflow - can Redwood accept a customer-managed key? We have strict key rotation policies.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported; we just need the key ARN and a service principal to be added to the key policy. There might be a small step where we request decrypt permissions for the service account.
[01:54] Sofia Li: also audit logs, retention, that stuff - SOC2, right?
[02:00] Jordan Lee: we will share SOC2 and the auditor report; we keep request-level audit logs and can provide retention options.
[02:08] Maya Patel: Great. Priya, can you walk the numbers from the last run?
[02:15] Priya Menon: Sure. So last night we ran the model variant redwood-llama-2-13b-q4 with int8 quantization on a single dedicated GPU node. The avg p50 latency across the 200 sample prompts was around 220 ms per request end-to-end, p95 about 520 ms. Token generation cost looked like roughly 0.9 cents per 1k tokens in that config, but that's a rough estimate.
[02:48] Ethan Ross: Hmm 220 ms p50 is pretty good. Is that including prefix KV cache hits?
[02:55] Priya Menon: yes, most of our runs used the prefix caching, which helps since you said many prompts share a similar preamble. We can send raw logs; note some lines in the log show the kv cache as k-v cash in the auto transcript sorry, it's not actually cash.
[03:15] Jordan Lee: ha, yeah transcription artifacts. There's also the batching setting- we used micro-batching of 8 to keep latency low.
[03:26] Maya Patel: For our use case latency spike at p95 is our biggest concern. Are there knob we can tune?
[03:33] Priya Menon: We can tune batching (lower batch size to reduce p95), or move to more dedicated nodes (more shards) or reduce quantization aggressiveness if hallucination risk is high. There's a tradeoff: smaller batch = higher cost per token.
[03:48] Liam O'Neal: On cost, we need to see hosted vs dedicated numbers. We don't want to overcommit to dedicated unless throughput needs it.
[03:56] Jordan Lee: sensible. We'll put a cost table in the benchmark sheet comparing per-token costs across hosted, dedicated, and a hybrid route that routes infrequent requests to hosted.
[04:06] Ethan Ross: About data residency — our production data resides in eu-west-1, can Redwood pin region?
[04:12] Priya Menon: Yup, you can pin region or route by policy; for the POC we'll run in eu-west-1 staging and then mirror for prod.
[04:22] Sofia Li: On the KMS key policy, do you need an IAM role or service principal? We prefer role assumption.
[04:29] Jordan Lee: Either works. We typically ask for a role with kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions and a principal for our service account if you want to add a principal.
[04:40] Maya Patel: Okay next, the staging dataset — we prepared 200 prompts with a mix of short and long contexts. We'll scrub pii but keep the context distribution similar to prod.
[04:51] Priya Menon: Perfect. Please include prompts that exercise long-context behavior; that will surface kv cache and compilation differences.
[05:01] Jordan Lee: quick note on compilation: the runtime may choose different kernels depending on sequence length distribution; that can change latency.
[05:10] Liam O'Neal: We had an internal question about private deployments: if we go private on-prem, what's the onboarding time?
[05:17] Priya Menon: Private on-prem typically 8-12 weeks depending on network and compliance gating; private VPC deployment is 3-6 weeks usually.
[05:25] Ethan Ross: that's a big delta. For POC we want to keep hosted/dedicated options.
[05:30] Jordan Lee: totally. We'll avoid long lead time commitments until you validate performance.
[05:35] Priya Menon: On telemetry, we'll push detailed per-token latency and per-request trace links to the runbook for the 500-req test. Expect raw logs as gzipped JSON.
[05:48] Maya Patel: Can Redwood's runtime do prefix caching across requests from different users? Some of our prompts share shared system prompt.
[05:57] Priya Menon: Yes prefix/KV caching can be configured for shared prefixes, but you need consistent cache keys; we'll add recommendations in the runbook.
[06:06] Sofia Li: Any compliance gaps we should know about before we sign an NDA?
[06:12] Jordan Lee: We'll send the security questionnaire. Generally we support SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS options. For healthcare-specific HITRUST we haven't got full cert yet but there's an assessment path.
[06:28] Ethan Ross: Ok -- timeline check: when can Priya kick off the 500 sample latency test?
[06:33] Priya Menon: I can start tomorrow once Ethan completes peering and Sofia provides KMS ARN. We'll probably run the test overnight to capture tail behavior.
[06:43] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll send the benchmark spreadsheet immediately after this call and include a cost comparison and the suggested config for micro-batching and kv cache settings.
[06:55] Maya Patel: On expected outcomes: if p95 is under 700 ms and cost within target, we'll move to a 2-week pilot with production traffic mirror.
[07:05] Jordan Lee: noted. We'll also include rollback/fallback policy in the runbook in case of regression.
[07:12] Priya Menon: small note: one of the runs had a weird tokenization diff causing slightly different token counts vs your local tokenizer. We'll include tokenizer version and seed in the logs.
[07:25] Ethan Ross: good call, tokenizer mismatches have bitten us before.
[07:30] Maya Patel: ok final recap?
[07:33] Jordan Lee: recap: Ethan to finish peering and send peering ID; Sofia to provide KMS key ARN and key policy guidance; Maya to send 200 sample prompts scrubbed; Jordan to send benchmark sheet and SOC2 docs; Priya to run 500-req latency run once access is ready and upload logs. Next sync same time next week unless earlier needed.
[07:58] Liam O'Neal: sounds good, thanks.
[08:02] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[08:08] (call ends)
